slides.0.title: Mendoza II: the Uco Valley
slides.0.subtitle: Tupungato, Tunuyán, San Carlos, and Gualtallary, Paraje Altamira and La Consulta
slides.1.title: The Uco Valley at a glance
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Location
slides.1.highlights.0.content: About 100 km southwest of Mendoza city, stretching some 70 km north to south along the Tunuyán River (Wine With Seth)
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Rapid growth
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Vineyard area grew from under 10,000 ha in 2000 to over 29,000 ha today
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Altitude and climate
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Vineyards at about 900 to over 1,700 m; mean annual temperature about 14°C, a summer day-night swing of up to 20°C, and under 250 mm of rain a year
slides.1.content: The Uco Valley is the high-altitude rising heart of Argentine wine.
slides.2.title: Three departments and their districts
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Tupungato (north)
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Gualtallary, Tupungato Alto and others, at about 1,100–1,600 m
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Tunuyán (centre)
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Vista Flores, San Pablo and Los Chacayes
slides.2.highlights.2.title: San Carlos (south)
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Paraje Altamira, Pampa El Cepillo, Eugenio Bustos and La Consulta (whose GI status is still under evaluation)
slides.2.content: Remember the north-to-south order: Tupungato, Tunuyán, San Carlos.
slides.3.title: Soils, style and GIs
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Calcareous soils
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Alluvial soils of stone and sand rich in calcium carbonate at the surface; limestone caliche reaches up to 40% in select Gualtallary blocks
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Varieties and style
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Malbec dominates with fresh red and violet fruit, bright acidity and chalky minerality; Cabernet Franc is second; limestone blocks in Gualtallary give mineral Chardonnay
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Geographical indications
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Paraje Altamira (2013) is called Argentina's first terroir-defined GI; San Pablo, Pampa El Cepillo and Los Chacayes followed (2019 each); Gualtallary is pending (Wine With Seth)
slides.3.content: The Uco Valley's signature is altitude plus limestone: fresh, mineral and tightly structured.
In north-to-south order, the three departments of the Uco Valley are?
From north to south: Tupungato, Tunuyán, San Carlos.
In which department is Paraje Altamira?
It lies in southern San Carlos.
What is the key feature of Uco Valley soils?
A. Surface layers rich in calcium carbonate
Alluvial stone and sand rich in calcium carbonate at the surface.
